Thoughtful dataset curation with principled VRF and HACF filtering stages to reduce VLM hallucinations and ensure grounding quality
Addresses documented entropy collapse problem in RL-based IQA (VisualQuality-R1: 2.04% unique scores vs 71.34% ground truth) with targeted KL-Coverage regularizer
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: seven datasets across three categories, extensive baselines, VLM-as-judge evaluation, downstream task validation, and thorough ablations
Consistent empirical improvements, particularly on reasoning quality metrics (Table 2: 8.72 vs 7.29 accuracy; significantly better on Reasonableness, Completeness, Confidence)
Practical utility demonstrated through downstream task evaluation (image restoration), showing that better reasoning enables better guidance for other models
Well-structured methodology with logical two-stage training pipeline (SFT for format, RL for policy)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 1 problem motivation, Figure 4 qualitative comparison, comprehensive supplementary materials)
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: applies standard techniques (SFT + GRPO from prior work) with engineering contributions (filtering, KL-Coverage regularizer) rather than conceptual innovations; base model is standard VLM

Incomplete evaluation of region grounding effectiveness: no quantitative validation that generated bounding boxes are semantically meaningful or align with human selections; missing analysis of when cropping actually helps vs. hurts

KL-Coverage regularizer design choices lack justification: targeting only numerical tokens seems ad-hoc; simple covariance metric (Eq. 1) without principled motivation; variable improvements across datasets (Table 3) with no analysis; hyperparameter p=0.02 appears arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

Reasoning quality evaluation primarily through VLM-as-judge which is subject to evaluator biases; higher scores may reflect verbosity rather than correctness; no human studies or quantitative verification that identified regions explain quality scores

Incomplete experimental documentation: filtering statistics not provided (what fraction filtered out?); progressive resampling strategy vaguely described; no inference time or computational overhead analysis despite iterative nature; typical iteration counts not reported
Missing failure analysis: qualitative examples appear selective; when does Zoom-IQA fail? What image types or distortions cause problems? Do crops sometimes target irrelevant regions?
Modest empirical improvements over VisualQuality-R1 in score regression (Table 1: 0.938 vs 0.910 on KonIQ; often 2-3% gains), limiting impact despite reasoning improvements

Generalization concerns: trained on real-world images (KonIQ); weaker results on AGIQA suggest challenges with AI-generated content; inconsistent improvements across synthetic distortion datasets suggest dataset-specific factors
Reproducibility limitations: depends on closed-source Gemini and proprietary Qwen model; some hyperparameters underspecified; no code/data release mentioned
Statistical significance testing absent from Table 1 comparisons; interaction between multiple reward signals and KL regularizer not thoroughly analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies that existing VLM-based IQA methods lack interactive region-aware reasoning, with clear distinction from VQA-style grounding.
Careful dataset curation: GR-IQA pipeline with VRF and HACF thoughtfully designed to mitigate VLM hallucination—a real technical challenge.
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests on 7 benchmarks, includes ablation study (Table 3), qualitative comparisons, and demonstrates downstream application to image restoration.
Two-stage framework design: Conceptually sound separation of 'how to zoom' (SFT) and 'when to zoom' (RL) addresses a genuine challenge.
Reasoning quality evaluation methodology: VLM-as-judge approach (Table 2) with four criteria is methodologically reasonable for assessing description quality.
weaknesses: Marginal empirical improvements: Gains over Q-Insight/VisualQuality-R1 are ~2% (KonIQ: 0.938 vs. 0.918; SPAQ: actually worse at 0.902 vs. 0.903). These do not justify the added complexity of interactive reasoning and RL training.

Experimental design concerns: Authors retrained VisualQuality-R1 due to missing KonIQ checkpoint—unclear if hyperparameter tuning matched Zoom-IQA's development effort. No statistical significance testing despite small margins (<2%). Mixed base models across baselines.

Dataset scale and methodology: 7,000 samples is small by 2024 standards. Heterogeneous model usage (Gemini→Qwen filter→Qwen train) risks model-specific biases. VRF thresholds (rating diff <0.05, IoU >0.5, entropy <0.01) unexplained; no sensitivity analysis or ablation.

KL-Coverage regularizer justified insufficiently: Choice of p=0.02 for token masking lacks justification. Connection between 'log-probability-logit covariance' and the penalty is not rigorously established. Ablation in Table 3 conflates KL with progressive training.

Reasoning quality evaluation is indirect and biased: Relies on closed-source VLM judges (Gemini, GPT-5-mini) without inter-rater agreement or human validation. No ground truth for whether VLM scores align with human preferences.

Restoration results lack quantitative rigor: Figures 7-9 are qualitative only; no metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS). Only 3 images shown. Setup may not be fair (DreamClear not designed for these reasoning formats).

Reproducibility blocked by closed-source models: Data generation (Gemini-2.5-pro) and evaluation (GPT-5-mini) cannot be reproduced. No code release mentioned. Progressive re-sampling strategy details vague.
Limited technical novelty: SFT + RL with GRPO is standard practice. KL-Coverage is incremental regularization. Main novelty is application to IQA rather than algorithmic innovation.
Overstated generalization claims: 'Impressive zero-shot generalization' tested on only one downstream task (restoration). AGIQA scores (0.816/0.765) not particularly strong. No true OOD evaluation.
Missing critical comparisons: No ablation of simple baselines (fixed cropping, averaging crops). No inference time comparison. No analysis of how performance scales with GR-IQA dataset size.

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies and addresses a real limitation of existing VLM-based IQA methods—their non-interactive nature—with good grounding in human behavior (DiffIQA zoom feature)

Thoughtful technical engineering: VRF creatively addresses hallucination detection specific to IQA; HACF provides practical filtering; KL-Coverage regularizer directly tackles documented mode collapse in RL-trained LLMs; two-stage pipeline is well-motivated

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Assessed across 7 benchmarks in 3 categories with 3 evaluation perspectives (score regression, reasoning quality, downstream application); thorough ablation study demonstrating component contributions; convincing qualitative examples
Dataset contribution: GR-IQA dataset with ~7,000 carefully curated reasoning trajectories could be valuable for future research
Solid execution: Clear presentation with effective visualizations, implementation details and hyperparameters provided, good reproducibility
Demonstrates practical value: Shows region-aware reasoning can guide downstream tasks like image restoration with improved results
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: SFT+RL with GRPO is standard practice in VLM literature; region-aware reasoning with cropping parallels established VQA work; KL-Coverage regularizer applies straightforward KL penalties to suppress covariance—engineering contribution rather than fundamental innovation

Marginal quantitative improvements: Many gains <1% over baselines (e.g., KonIQ: 0.938 vs 0.918, KADID: 0.701 vs 0.702); critically, no statistical significance testing (no error bars, confidence intervals, or p-values) to validate improvements are not within noise

GR-IQA dataset lacks human validation: No human studies confirming that Gemini-generated reasoning aligns with actual human reasoning paths; relies entirely on automated filtering heuristics; VRF's approach to hallucination detection may miss plausible-sounding but incorrect descriptions; filtering statistics (percentage of data removed) not reported

Problematic reasoning quality evaluation: VLM-as-judge (Table 2) evaluation lacks independent ground truth and inter-annotator agreement; no comparison with human judges; subjective metrics (Accuracy, Reasonableness, etc.) may favor longer, more detailed outputs regardless of reasoning quality; no established definition of 'correct' reasoning in IQA

Interactive reasoning mechanism not systematically validated: No quantitative analysis of whether cropping decisions are appropriate, whether iterative refinement actually improves accuracy (only shows it occurs), or whether benefits derive from region awareness vs. multi-turn attention; qualitative examples demonstrate cropping but not necessity

Generalization concerns: All training on KonIQ-derived splits; limited zero-shot evaluation; no analysis of generalization to underrepresented distortion types; no evaluation on truly out-of-distribution test sets
Incomplete ablations: Missing comparison to Gemini-2.5-pro baseline without fine-tuning; no separate impact analysis of VRF vs. HACF filtering; no analysis of cropping frequency calibration effects
Downstream task evaluation incomplete: Image restoration results (Figure 5) qualitative only without quantitative metrics; application feels orthogonal to core IQA evaluation
Lack of computational cost analysis: No inference time or memory comparisons against baselines

Technical design choices underspecified: Why p=0.02 for KL-Coverage token selection? Sensitivity analysis missing; rationale for targeting numerical tokens only unclear; progressive resampling strategy details incomplete

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clear articulation of why existing VLM-based IQA methods lack interactivity and visual grounding; compelling analogy to human assessment behavior
Thoughtful dataset curation: VRF and HACF filtering pipeline creatively addresses hallucination without modifying inputs, avoiding IQA-specific evaluation pitfalls

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Seven datasets across three categories, multiple evaluation perspectives (score regression, reasoning quality, downstream application, saliency grounding), thorough ablations demonstrating component contributions

Technical depth and clarity: KL-Coverage regularizer well-motivated for preventing entropy collapse; progressive re-sampling intelligently handles imbalanced distributions; clear problem formulation with structured prompts

Excellent presentation and transparency: Strong qualitative examples effectively demonstrate region-aware reasoning advantages; extensive supplementary material; robustness discussion with concrete examples
Practical utility demonstrated: Downstream application to image restoration (SUPIR, DreamClear) shows real-world value; saliency grounding benchmark validates semantic meaningfulness of crops
weaknesses: Marginal and inconsistent empirical improvements: KonIQ improvement of only +0.028 over VisualQuality-R1; PIPAL performance slightly underperforms some baselines; gains within plausible noise margins of VLM non-determinism

Dataset curation reproducibility concerns: Filtering thresholds (0.05 rating diff, 0.5 IoU, 0.01 entropy) lack principled justification; final data retention rate not clearly reported; reliance on external models (Gemini, Qwen) complicates reproducibility; GR-IQA apparently not released

Indirect baseline comparisons: VisualQuality-R1 re-trained in-house; single-stage SFT baseline is strawman without equivalent-compute SFT-only comparison; missing comparisons with other region-based reasoning methods

Limited evaluation scope: Training only on KonIQ; no cross-dataset experiments; zero-shot generalization only indirectly tested via restoration; human evaluation extremely limited (15 annotators, 30 images); no systematic failure analysis

VLM-as-judge evaluation bias risk: Uses same model families (Gemini, Qwen, Grok) as system components; circular validation risk from similar architectural biases; insufficient independent validation despite human evaluation evidence

Limited technical novelty: Individual components relatively standard (KL penalties from PPO, entropy collapse mitigation from recent LLM work, two-stage training as common practice); crop generation via bbox straightforward; primary novelty is engineering combination rather than fundamental advance

Missing methodological details: Base model choice (Qwen2.5-VL-7b) not justified; hyperparameter sensitivity not explored; progressive re-sampling schedule not fully documented; training cost (especially RL stage) not discussed

Insufficient statistical rigor: No significance testing for reported improvements; confidence intervals absent; reasoning quality evaluation criteria ('Accuracy' prioritizing subjective human perception) somewhat circular for validating a metric itself

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies genuine limitation in VLM-based IQA methods lacking interactive region-aware reasoning with compelling analogy to human assessment
Thoughtful dataset curation: GR-IQA with VRF and HACF modules thoughtfully addresses VLM hallucination while preserving data integrity
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests on 7 diverse datasets, multiple baseline categories, ablations, downstream tasks, and qualitative analysis
Saliency grounding validation (Table 6): Demonstrates cropping mechanism focuses on semantically meaningful regions (Area 0.36 vs. 0.65 for baseline)
Good presentation: Well-structured writing with effective visual examples and clear motivation for region-aware reasoning
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: SFT+RL pipeline mirrors Q-Insight/VisualQuality-R1; KL-Coverage is straightforward token-level penalty; core cropping mechanism is mechanically simple

Marginal empirical improvements without significance testing: KonIQ 0.938 vs 0.918, KADID tied at 0.701, PIPAL 0.468 vs 0.458; no statistical significance reported; differences potentially within noise

Serious evaluation bias: VLM-as-judge (Table 2) uses Gemini to evaluate Gemini-trained outputs, introducing inherent bias; human evaluation (Table 7) limited to 30 images with 15 annotators; 1-9 subjective scale hard to interpret
Circular dataset dependency: GR-IQA created via Gemini labeling of KonIQ, then used to fine-tune model; comparison fairness unclear if baselines lacked access to synthetic labels

Unjustified hyperparameters: VRF thresholds (0.05, 0.5, 0.01) lack ablation; KL-Coverage p=0.02 unexplained; reward weights (αscore=1, αrank=2) appear arbitrary; progressive resampling poorly detailed

Weak claim substantiation: 'Unreliable reasoning' argument relies on qualitative cherry-picked examples; VisualQuality-R1 'score collapse' (2.04% unique) unexplained (implementation issue vs. fundamental limitation)
Missing error analysis: No investigation of failure modes, when cropping helps/hurts, or cross-dataset generalization; runtime overhead 1.5-3× (0.06s vs 0.02-0.05s) unaddressed
Methodological concerns: No systematic analysis of when region grounding is beneficial; dataset filtering biases toward clear cases; unclear if learned crop policy generalizes to non-KonIQ domains

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates the limitation of non-interactive IQA methods and effectively motivates iterative region-aware reasoning with human cognition analogy
Thoughtful dataset contribution: GR-IQA with novel VRF and HACF filtering techniques addresses VLM hallucination in a principled way, avoiding the pitfall of adding distortions for IQA assessment
Technically sound two-stage pipeline: SFT+RL approach is well-designed; KL-Coverage regularizer effectively addresses mode collapse in numerical token generation with targeted design

Comprehensive experimental validation: 7 datasets across 3 categories, quantitative metrics (PLCC/SRCC), reasoning quality via multiple VLM evaluators, human study, downstream tasks (restoration), and thorough ablations

Strong reasoning quality results: Qualitative comparisons convincingly demonstrate more specific, accurate reasoning with precise region localization compared to baselines, which may matter more than raw score improvements

Practical utility demonstrated: Downstream task results on image restoration (SUPIR, DreamClear) show real-world applicability; saliency grounding analysis (Table 6) validates semantic meaningfulness of crops
Reproducibility-focused: Detailed implementation details, extensive prompt documentation in appendix, ablation studies, and discussion of robustness (bokeh, low-light) support reproduction
Clear presentation of main ideas: Figures 1-4 effectively communicate the approach; supplementary material is well-organized
weaknesses: Modest quantitative improvements without significance testing: PLCC gains of 0.010-0.020 (e.g., 0.938 vs 0.918 on KonIQ) are marginal and lack error bars or p-values; may be within noise given typical variance

Limited core methodological novelty: Individual components (VLMs, RL, KL penalties, progressive training) are established; novelty lies in application/combination rather than fundamental innovation; cropping concept is straightforward

Computational efficiency concerns: 1.5-3× inference latency increase (0.06s vs 0.02-0.05s) without proportional score improvements; cost-benefit trade-off not adequately justified for practical deployment

Arbitrary dataset construction choices: Filtering thresholds (rating diff 0.05, bbox IoU 0.5, entropy diff 0.01) lack principled justification; no sensitivity analysis; missing statistics on rejection rates per stage; limited inter-annotator agreement metrics

Incomplete analysis of cropping behavior: Limited investigation of when/why zooming is beneficial; no systematic exploration of failure modes or case analysis by degradation type; single baseline (center crop) for learned policy comparison

Unjustified methodological choices: Algorithm selection (GRPO over alternatives) not motivated; reward weight coefficients arbitrary; structured format design not formally justified; no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis

Evaluation concerns: VLM-as-judge evaluation uses Gemini as primary (though addressed with Grok + human); human ranking limited to 15 annotators × 30 images; no statistical significance testing across results

Limited generalization analysis: Single base model (Qwen2.5-VL-7b); unclear sensitivity to VLM architecture; no robustness analysis across RL hyperparameters; still-image only; unclear applicability beyond IQA

Incomplete presentation: 'Uncertainty-aware reasoning' in title not formally defined; relationship between reasoning reliability and visual grounding could be more explicit; some dense sections reduce clarity
Missing failure analysis and ablations: No systematic investigation of when cropping hurts; limited exploration of which distortion types benefit most; single train set (KonIQ) investigated
